\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{சூதாடு} (cūtāṭu)}{சூதாடு (cūtāṭu)}]{\ta{சூதாடு} (cūtāṭu) — to gamble}

\label{lesson:TA-C544-cutatu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for privacy, then the Tamil for to test.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{சூதாடு}}
\textbf{\ta{சூதாடு}} — \emph{cūtāṭu} — \textquotedblleft{}to gamble\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{சூதாடினால்} \ta{பணத்தை} \ta{இழப்பாய்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{cūtāṭiṉāl paṇattai iḻappāy.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you gamble, you will lose money.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{சூதாடினேன்}, \emph{cūtāṭiṉēṉ}.

\ta{சூது} \textquotedblleft{}gambling\textquotedblright{} + \ta{ஆடு} (\emph{āṭu}) \textquotedblleft{}to play\textquotedblright{}. Gambling as a habit is \ta{சூதாட்டம்}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{சூதாடு}} (\emph{cūtāṭu}) joins \ta{சூது} (\emph{cūtu}), \textquotedblleft{}gambling\textquotedblright{}, from Sanskrit \emph{dyūta} (CDIAL 6608), and the native \ta{ஆடு} (\emph{āṭu}), \textquotedblleft{}to play\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cūtāṭu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cūtāṭu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cūtāṭiṉāl paṇattai iḻappāy.} — If you gamble, you will lose money.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for privacy, then the Tamil for to test, then say \emph{cūtāṭu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{சூதாடு} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To gamble\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{பணயம்} \ta{வை} (paṇayam vai)}{பணயம் வை (paṇayam vai)}]{\ta{பணயம்} \ta{வை} (paṇayam vai) — to stake; to risk}

\label{lesson:TA-C544-panayam-vai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to test, then the Tamil for to gamble.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{பணயம்} \ta{வை}}
\textbf{\ta{பணயம்} \ta{வை}} — \emph{paṇayam vai} — \textquotedblleft{}to stake; to risk\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{அவர்} \ta{தன்} \ta{வீட்டையே} \ta{பணயம்} \ta{வைத்தார்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avar taṉ vīṭṭaiyē paṇayam vaittār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He staked even his own house.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{பணயம்} \ta{வைத்தேன்}, \emph{paṇayam vaittēṉ}.

What is staked takes -\ta{ஐ}. The ending -\ta{ஏ} gives \textquotedblleft{}even\textquotedblright{}: \ta{வீட்டையே}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{பணயம்} \ta{வை}} (\emph{paṇayam vai}) joins \ta{பணயம்} (\emph{paṇayam}), \textquotedblleft{}a stake\textquotedblright{}, from Sanskrit \emph{paṇa}, \textquotedblleft{}a wager, a stake\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 7714), and the native light verb \ta{வை}, \textquotedblleft{}to put\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paṇayam vai}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paṇayam vai}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avar taṉ vīṭṭaiyē paṇayam vaittār.} — He staked even his own house.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to test, then the Tamil for to gamble, then say \emph{paṇayam vai} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{பணயம்} \ta{வை} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To stake; to risk\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{சாகசம்} (cākacam)}{சாகசம் (cākacam)}]{\ta{சாகசம்} (cākacam) — an adventure; a daring feat}

\label{lesson:TA-C544-cakacam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to gamble, then the Tamil for to stake.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{சாகசம்}}
\textbf{\ta{சாகசம்}} — \emph{cākacam} — \textquotedblleft{}an adventure; a daring feat\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{மலையில்} \ta{ஏறுவது} \ta{அவனுக்கு} \ta{ஒரு} \ta{சாகசம்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{malaiyil ēṟuvatu avaṉukku oru cākacam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
For him, climbing a mountain is an adventure.
\end{quote}

Daring stunts in a circus or a film are \ta{சாகசங்கள்}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{சாகசம்}} (\emph{cākacam}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{sāhasa}, \textquotedblleft{}boldness, daring\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13378); Tamil writes the \emph{h} as \ta{க}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cākacam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cākacam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{malaiyil ēṟuvatu avaṉukku oru cākacam.} — For him, climbing a mountain is an adventure.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to gamble, then the Tamil for to stake, then say \emph{cākacam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{சாகசம்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An adventure; a daring feat\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{சகுனம்} (cakuṉam)}{சகுனம் (cakuṉam)}]{\ta{சகுனம்} (cakuṉam) — an omen}

\label{lesson:TA-C544-cakunam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to stake, then the Tamil for an adventure.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{சகுனம்}}
\textbf{\ta{சகுனம்}} — \emph{cakuṉam} — \textquotedblleft{}an omen\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{பூனை} \ta{குறுக்கே} \ta{போனால்} \ta{கெட்ட} \ta{சகுனம்} \ta{என்று} \ta{சிலர்} \ta{நம்புகிறார்கள்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pūṉai kuṟukkē pōṉāl keṭṭa cakuṉam eṉṟu cilar nampukiṟārkaḷ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Some people believe that a cat crossing your path is a bad omen.
\end{quote}

Good and bad omens: \ta{நல்ல} \ta{சகுனம்}, \ta{கெட்ட} \ta{சகுனம்}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{சகுனம்}} (\emph{cakuṉam}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{śakuna}, \textquotedblleft{}a bird\textquotedblright{}, and so a sign read from birds, an omen (CDIAL 12245).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cakuṉam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cakuṉam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pūṉai kuṟukkē pōṉāl keṭṭa cakuṉam eṉṟu cilar nampukiṟārkaḷ.} — Some people believe that a cat crossing your path is a bad omen.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to stake, then the Tamil for an adventure, then say \emph{cakuṉam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{சகுனம்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An omen\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{விவேகம்} (vivēkam)}{விவேகம் (vivēkam)}]{\ta{விவேகம்} (vivēkam) — prudence; good sense}

\label{lesson:TA-C544-vivekam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for an adventure, then the Tamil for an omen.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{விவேகம்}}
\textbf{\ta{விவேகம்}} — \emph{vivēkam} — \textquotedblleft{}prudence; good sense\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{அவசரத்தில்} \ta{முடிவு} \ta{எடுப்பது} \ta{விவேகம்} \ta{அல்ல}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avacarattil muṭivu eṭuppatu vivēkam alla.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Deciding in a hurry is not prudent.
\end{quote}

The opposite of rashness. A -\ta{அம்} noun: \ta{விவேகத்துடன்}, with good sense.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{விவேகம்}} (\emph{vivēkam}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{viveka}, \textquotedblleft{}discrimination, consideration\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with the Tamil ending -\ta{அம்}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vivēkam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vivēkam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avacarattil muṭivu eṭuppatu vivēkam alla.} — Deciding in a hurry is not prudent.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for an adventure, then the Tamil for an omen, then say \emph{vivēkam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{விவேகம்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Prudence; good sense\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Threads and Beads to Luck and Daring}

\label{lesson:TA-R544-review-538-544}



\begin{quote}
Say the Tamil for to knit and to weave.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item to knit, to weave, to string, a loom, silk
  \item a flute, a veena, to play an instrument, to pluck strings, to compose music
  \item a concert, a stage play, a stage, a rehearsal, make-up
  \item insurance, a risk, danger, an agent, bail
  \item a guarantee, validity, a seal, to swear an oath, to grant
  \item an official order, strict, a fingerprint, privacy, to test
  \item to gamble, to stake, an adventure, an omen, prudence
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To knit? (\textbf{\ta{பின்னு}}, \emph{piṉṉu}.) To weave? (\textbf{\ta{முடை}}, \emph{muṭai}.) To string? (\textbf{\ta{கோர்}}, \emph{kōr}.) A loom? (\textbf{\ta{தறி}}, \emph{taṟi}.) Silk? (\textbf{\ta{பட்டு}}, \emph{paṭṭu}.) A flute? (\textbf{\ta{புல்லாங்குழல்}}, \emph{pullāṅkuḻal}.) A veena? (\textbf{\ta{வீணை}}, \emph{vīṇai}.) To play an instrument? (\textbf{\ta{வாசி}}, \emph{vāci}.) To pluck strings? (\textbf{\ta{மீட்டு}}, \emph{mīṭṭu}.) To compose music? (\textbf{\ta{இசையமை}}, \emph{icaiyamai}.) A concert? (\textbf{\ta{கச்சேரி}}, \emph{kaccēri}.) A stage play? (\textbf{\ta{நாடகம்}}, \emph{nāṭakam}.) A stage? (\textbf{\ta{மேடை}}, \emph{mēṭai}.) A rehearsal? (\textbf{\ta{ஒத்திகை}}, \emph{ottikai}.) Make-up? (\textbf{\ta{ஒப்பனை}}, \emph{oppaṉai}.) Insurance? (\textbf{\ta{காப்பீடு}}, \emph{kāppīṭu}.) A risk? (\textbf{\ta{இடர்}}, \emph{iṭar}.) Danger? (\textbf{\ta{அபாயம்}}, \emph{apāyam}.) An agent? (\textbf{\ta{முகவர்}}, \emph{mukavar}.) Bail? (\textbf{\ta{பிணை}}, \emph{piṇai}.) A guarantee? (\textbf{\ta{உத்தரவாதம்}}, \emph{uttaravātam}.) Validity? (\textbf{\ta{செல்லுபடி}}, \emph{cellupaṭi}.) A seal? (\textbf{\ta{முத்திரை}}, \emph{muttirai}.) To swear an oath? (\textbf{\ta{சத்தியம்} \ta{செய்}}, \emph{cattiyam cey}.) To grant? (\textbf{\ta{அளி}}, \emph{aḷi}.) An official order? (\textbf{\ta{கட்டளை}}, \emph{kaṭṭaḷai}.) Strict? (\textbf{\ta{கடுமையான}}, \emph{kaṭumaiyāṉa}.) A fingerprint? (\textbf{\ta{கைரேகை}}, \emph{kairēkai}.) Privacy? (\textbf{\ta{தனியுரிமை}}, \emph{taṉiyurimai}.) To test? (\textbf{\ta{சோதி}}, \emph{cōti}.) To gamble? (\textbf{\ta{சூதாடு}}, \emph{cūtāṭu}.) To stake? (\textbf{\ta{பணயம்} \ta{வை}}, \emph{paṇayam vai}.) An adventure? (\textbf{\ta{சாகசம்}}, \emph{cākacam}.) An omen? (\textbf{\ta{சகுனம்}}, \emph{cakuṉam}.) Prudence? (\textbf{\ta{விவேகம்}}, \emph{vivēkam}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
